01-01.title: Circumcision of Christ and Saint Basil
01-01.text: The eighth day after the Nativity commemorates Christ receiving the covenantal sign and the name Jesus. Basil the Great, the fourth-century Cappadocian bishop and theologian, is also honored.

01-06.title: Holy Theophany
01-06.text: The baptism of Christ in the Jordan reveals the Trinity: the Son is baptized, the Spirit descends, and the Father bears witness.

01-17.title: Anthony the Great
01-17.text: Anthony of Egypt became a foundational model of desert monasticism. His ascetic witness shaped Christian monastic practice far beyond Egypt.

01-30.title: The Three Hierarchs
01-30.text: Basil the Great, Gregory the Theologian, and John Chrysostom are commemorated together as teachers whose different gifts serve one Gospel.

02-02.title: Meeting of the Lord
02-02.text: Forty days after the Nativity, Christ is brought to the Temple. Simeon and Anna recognize Him as light and salvation.

02-10.title: Hieromartyr Charalambos
02-10.text: Charalambos is remembered as an aged bishop and martyr whose endurance became a lasting witness to courage and pastoral faithfulness.

03-09.title: Forty Martyrs of Sebaste
03-09.text: Forty Christian soldiers were exposed on a frozen lake after refusing to renounce Christ. Their shared witness became an image of perseverance.

03-25.title: Annunciation
03-25.text: Gabriel announces the Incarnation to Mary. Her free assent stands at the center of the feast: divine initiative meets human trust.

04-23.title: Great Martyr George
04-23.text: George is honored as a military martyr. The dragon image developed as a symbol of the victory of faith over evil.

05-21.title: Constantine and Helen
05-21.text: Constantine and his mother Helen are honored for ending imperial persecution, supporting the Church, and strengthening Christian memory in Jerusalem.

06-24.title: Nativity of John the Baptist
06-24.text: The birth of the Forerunner is celebrated six months before the Nativity of Christ. His life points toward repentance and the Messiah.

06-29.title: Peter and Paul
06-29.text: Peter and Paul embody distinct apostolic callings joined in one mission, remembering leadership, repentance, missionary labor, and martyrdom.

07-11.title: Great Martyr Euphemia
07-11.text: Euphemia of Chalcedon is remembered for martyrdom and for later Orthodox tradition associating her relics with the Council of Chalcedon.

07-20.title: Prophet Elijah
07-20.text: Elijah confronts idolatry and injustice while revealing both divine power and the quiet voice of God.

07-22.title: Mary Magdalene
07-22.text: Mary Magdalene is honored as a myrrhbearer and witness of the Resurrection, called Equal-to-the-Apostles in Eastern tradition.

07-27.title: Panteleimon the Healer
07-27.text: Panteleimon is remembered as a physician who placed healing at the service of mercy and is invoked among the holy unmercenary healers.

08-06.title: Transfiguration
08-06.text: On Mount Tabor, the disciples behold Christ’s glory. The feast proclaims that divine light transforms rather than destroys human nature.

08-15.title: Dormition of the Theotokos
08-15.text: The Church commemorates the falling asleep of Mary and celebrates death transformed by communion with Christ.

08-29.title: Beheading of John the Baptist
08-29.text: John’s death at Herod’s command is remembered as the cost of speaking moral truth to power. The day is traditionally kept as a strict fast.

09-01.title: Beginning of the Church Year
09-01.text: September 1 opens the ecclesiastical year in Byzantine tradition, gathering themes of creation, providence, worship, and sanctified time.

09-08.title: Nativity of the Theotokos
09-08.text: The birth of Mary to Joachim and Anna begins the immediate preparation for the Incarnation and celebrates hope after long waiting.

09-14.title: Elevation of the Cross
09-14.text: The Cross is raised for veneration as the sign of Christ’s victory through self-giving love. The feast is observed with fasting.

09-24.title: Protomartyr Thecla
09-24.text: Thecla is honored as a disciple of Paul, an ascetic, and the first woman given the title Protomartyr in the Church’s devotional memory.

09-26.title: John the Theologian
09-26.text: The apostle and evangelist is remembered for placing incarnation, truth, love, and communion at the center of Christian life.

10-18.title: Evangelist Luke
10-18.text: Luke is traditionally received as the author of the Gospel and Acts, emphasizing mercy, prayer, the Holy Spirit, and mission.

10-26.title: Great Martyr Demetrius
10-26.text: Demetrius of Thessalonica is one of the most beloved military martyrs of the Christian East and is closely bound to his city.

11-01.title: Cosmas and Damian
11-01.text: The physician saints are remembered for healing without demanding payment, presenting medicine as a ministry of mercy.

11-08.title: Synaxis of the Archangels
11-08.text: The Church honors Michael, Gabriel, and all bodiless powers, giving thanks for their service in the biblical story of salvation.

11-13.title: John Chrysostom
11-13.text: John became renowned for preaching, biblical interpretation, care for the poor, and resistance to abuses of power.

11-21.title: Entrance of the Theotokos
11-21.text: The feast presents Mary’s dedication to God and emphasizes preparation, holiness, and the mystery of the Incarnation.

11-24.title: Great Martyr Catherine
11-24.text: Catherine of Alexandria is remembered as a learned virgin martyr whose wisdom and steadfastness challenged coercion.

11-30.title: Andrew the First-Called
11-30.text: Andrew is called First-Called because the Gospel of John places him among the first disciples to follow Christ.

12-04.title: Great Martyr Barbara
12-04.text: Barbara is remembered as a young martyr whose confession brought her into conflict with family authority and imperial persecution.

12-05.title: Sabbas the Sanctified
12-05.text: Sabbas shaped Palestinian monasticism. His lavra became a major center of Orthodox worship and learning.

12-06.title: Nicholas the Wonderworker
12-06.text: Nicholas, Bishop of Myra, is remembered for pastoral courage, defense of the vulnerable, generosity, and miracles attributed to his intercession.

12-12.title: Spyridon the Wonderworker
12-12.text: Spyridon is remembered as a shepherd-bishop of simplicity, charity, and fidelity to the Nicene confession.

12-17.title: Daniel and the Three Youths
12-17.text: Their stories embody faithfulness under exile and imperial pressure and are prominent in preparation for the Nativity.

12-20.title: Ignatius of Antioch
12-20.text: Ignatius wrote influential letters while being taken to martyrdom in Rome, stressing unity, Eucharistic life, and steadfast witness.

12-25.title: Nativity of Christ
12-25.text: The Church celebrates the Word made flesh: the eternal Son enters human history in humility, renewing creation.

12-26.title: Synaxis of the Theotokos
12-26.text: On the day after the Nativity, the Church gathers especially in honor of Mary, through whom Christ received human nature.

12-27.title: Stephen the Protomartyr
12-27.text: Stephen, one of the first seven deacons, becomes the first martyr after the Resurrection and forgives his persecutors.
